diagnostic_evidence.quote: The criteria include the following optimization problems: absolute volume and S-optimality maximization; norm and condition minimization in the two-norm , Frobenius norm and Schatten $p$-norms for $p>2$; stable rank maximization; and the new criterion of relative volume maximization.
Although most subset selection criteria are NP hard, not all are. For example, a submatrix $\mc$ with minimal Frobenius norm can be computed in polynomial time

we were not able to do so for a few criteria, including Schatten $p$-norm minimization for $p>2$ (Section~\ref{s_twop}) and condition number minimization in Schatten $p$-norms for $p>2$ (Section~\ref{s_condno}).

issues.failure_explanation: The abstract lists 'norm and condition minimization in the two-norm, Frobenius norm and Schatten p-norms for p>2' among the criteria and then asserts that all of these criteria are NP hard and admit no PTAS. The paper itself contradicts this: minimizing the Frobenius norm of the selected submatrix is shown to be solvable in polynomial time (greedy selection of the smallest-norm columns; Table t_intro marks it 'No' for NP hard), so it is not NP hard; and no no-PTAS result is established for Schatten p-norm minimization (p>2) or Schatten-p/mixed-Schatten-p condition number minimization, which the introduction explicitly concedes. The prose thus claims both NP hardness and PTAS inapproximability for criteria the paper does not establish.

failure_location.quote: We show that these criteria are NP hard and do not admit polynomial time approximation schemes (PTAS).

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Reword the abstract to exclude Frobenius-norm minimization from the NP-hardness claim and to restrict or hedge the no-PTAS claim to the criteria for which it is proven (e.g., 'most of these criteria', naming the exceptions as the introduction does).
issues.overall_effect: The paper's advertised scope is overstated: readers are told Frobenius-norm minimization is NP hard (it is in P) and that all listed criteria lack a PTAS (unproven for several of them). No formal result is invalidated.
issues.title: Abstract overclaims NP hardness and no-PTAS, including polynomial-time-solvable Frobenius-norm minimization
issues.why_classification: A purely expository rewording; every theorem, proof, threshold and guarantee is unchanged.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: We make no assumptions on the dimensions $m$ and~$n$ of~$\ma$.

issues.failure_explanation: Cauchy interlacing on the principal submatrix C^T C of A^T A gives sigma_{n-k+j}(A) <= sigma_j(C) (with sigma_i(A) = 0 for i > min{m,n}), not sigma_{min{m,n}-k+j}(A) <= sigma_j(C). For m < n the stated lower bound fails: e.g., A = [[1,0,1,0,0],[0,1,0,1,0]] in R^{2x5} has sigma_1(A) = sigma_2(A) = sqrt(2), while the 2-column submatrix C = I_2 has sigma_1(C) = 1, so the claimed sigma_{min{m,n}-k+1}(A) = sigma_1(A) = sqrt(2) <= sigma_1(C) = 1 is false. The paper explicitly disclaims any assumptions on m and n.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Correct the lower index in (e_inter) from min{m,n}-k+j to n-k+j (with the convention sigma_i(A) = 0 for i > min{m,n}), or state (e_inter) under the hypothesis m >= n.
issues.overall_effect: The labelled assertion (e_inter) is false as a general statement about A in R^{m x n}. Its only invocations (proofs of Lemmas l_inter and l_inter2) apply it to an m x k matrix of rank k (so m >= k and min{m,k} = k), where the written index coincides with the correct one; those lemmas and everything downstream of them are unaffected.
issues.title: Stated singular-value interlacing (e_inter) is false for wide matrices (m < n)
issues.why_classification: A one-index local correction; both uses in the paper already sit in the tall regime where the stated form is valid, so no result, rate or scope is lost.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The decision problems: volume maximization and S-optimality maximization are NP hard.

issues.failure_explanation: The overview asserts that volume and S-optimality maximization are shown NP complete (i.e., in NP and NP hard). The linked result (Theorem t_voldec) and its proof establish only NP hardness via reduction from X3C; membership in NP (e.g., polynomial-time verifiability of vol(C) >= b or sopt(C) >= b for rational inputs) is never argued anywhere in the paper. The prose claims a stronger classification than the formal content supports.

failure_location.quote: We show that volume and S-optimality maximization are NP complete (Section~\ref{s_volume1})

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace 'NP complete' by 'NP hard' in the Section 3 overview (or additionally prove NP membership for these decision problems).
issues.overall_effect: Overstates the complexity classification established for the volume and S-optimality maximization decision problems.
issues.title: Section 3 overview claims NP completeness where only NP hardness is proven
issues.why_classification: A one-word correction aligns the prose with the proven theorem; nothing else depends on it.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: For $k=2$, two distinct sets can overlap in one or in two elements.

Hence, for matrices $\hat{\mc}_2$ with $k=2$ columns, (\ref{e_aux1}) implies that $\vol(\hat{\mc}_2)=\sigma_1(\hat{\mc}_2)\sigma_2(\hat{\mc}_2) = \tfrac{2}{\sqrt{3}}\sqrt{\tfrac{2}{3}}=\tfrac{2\sqrt{2}}{3}$.
Then any collection $\mathcal{K}$ of cardinality $k=M$ has at least two sets $\mathcal{K}_i$ and $\mathcal{K}_j$ with $i\neq j$ and a non-empty intersection.

issues.failure_explanation: The induction hypothesis is stated for all (k-1)-column matrices and the base case is asserted for all 2-column submatrices, but the base-case computation covers only overlapping pairs. In a false X3C instance with M >= 3, two disjoint sets can occur (no exact cover exists), and the corresponding 2-column submatrix is orthonormal with vol = 1 > 2*sqrt(2)/3, so the asserted base case and the induction hypothesis are false as stated. The setup only guarantees that each M-column submatrix contains SOME overlapping pair, but the proof never arranges the chain of submatrices so that the 2-column base is that pair (never removing a column outside the pair), so the valid monotonicity step vol([B,c]) <= vol(B) is never anchored at a true base case and the induction establishes nothing as written.

failure_location.quote: For matrices $\hat{\mc}_{k-1}$ with $k-1$ columns, assume that $\vol(\hat{\mc}_{k-1})\leq \tfrac{2\sqrt{2}}{3}$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Re-scope the induction to j-column submatrices containing a fixed overlapping pair and peel off columns outside that pair; since every M-column submatrix of a false instance contains such a pair and vol([B,c]) <= vol(B) for unit-norm c is already proven, the chain yields vol(C) <= 2*sqrt(2)/3 for all such C, preserving the theorem and threshold.
issues.overall_effect: The proof of Theorem t_vol (no PTAS for volume maximization within 2*sqrt(2)/3) is incomplete as written; Theorem t_sopt, whose proof derives its threshold directly from t_vol, inherits the gap.
issues.title: Volume no-PTAS proof: induction hypothesis is false and the overlapping pair is never tracked
issues.why_classification: The repair is a short, local re-quantification of the induction using only machinery already present in the proof; the statement, threshold and dependent t_sopt all survive unchanged.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: For $k=2$, two distinct sets can overlap in one or in two elements.
Then any collection $\mathcal{K}$ of cardinality $k=M$ has at least two sets $\mathcal{K}_i$ and $\mathcal{K}_j$ with $i\neq j$ and a non-empty intersection.

issues.failure_explanation: As in Theorem t_vol, the induction hypothesis is asserted for all (k-1)-column matrices while the base-case bound is computed only for overlapping pairs. A false X3C instance with M >= 3 can contain two disjoint sets, whose 2-column submatrix is orthonormal with two-norm 1 < 2/sqrt(3), so the hypothesis is false as stated. The proof never chains the valid interlacing step sigma_1(hat C_k) >= sigma_1(hat C_{k-1}) down to the overlapping pair guaranteed inside every M-column submatrix, so the lower bound ||C||_2 >= 2/sqrt(3) is not established as written.

failure_location.quote: For matrices $\hat{\mc}_{k-1}$ with $k-1$ columns, assume that $\|\hat{\mc}_{k-1}\|_2=\sigma_{1}(\hat{\mc}_{k-1})\geq 2/\sqrt{3}$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Re-scope the induction to submatrices containing a fixed overlapping pair (removing columns outside the pair); sigma_1-monotonicity under column addition then gives ||C||_2 >= 2/sqrt(3) for every M-column submatrix, preserving the theorem and threshold.
issues.overall_effect: The proof of Theorem t_2m (no PTAS for two-norm minimization within 2/sqrt(3)) is incomplete as written; Theorem t_sr (no PTAS for stable rank maximization), which applies this bound, inherits the gap.
issues.title: Two-norm no-PTAS proof: induction hypothesis is false for disjoint column pairs
issues.why_classification: Local re-quantification of the induction using the already-proven step; the statement, threshold and dependent t_sr survive unchanged.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Hence, for matrices $\hat{\mc}_2$ with two columns $\|\hat{\mc}_2^{\dagger}\|_2=1/\sigma_2(\hat{\mc}_2)\geq\sqrt{3/2}$.
For $k=2$, two distinct sets can overlap in one or in two elements.
Then any collection $\mathcal{K}$ of cardinality $k=M$ has at least two sets $\mathcal{K}_i$ and $\mathcal{K}_j$ with $i\neq j$ and a non-empty intersection.

issues.failure_explanation: The induction hypothesis is asserted for all (k-1)-column matrices, but the base-case bound 1/sigma_2 >= sqrt(3/2) is computed only for overlapping pairs; a disjoint pair in a false X3C instance (M >= 3) has ||hat C_2^dagger||_2 = 1 < sqrt(3/2), so the hypothesis is false as stated (the written hypothesis also equates ||hat C_{k-1}^dagger||_2 with sigma_{k-1} instead of its reciprocal). The proof never anchors the valid interlacing step sigma_{k-1}(hat C_{k-1}) >= sigma_k(hat C_k) at the overlapping pair guaranteed inside every M-column submatrix, so ||C^dagger||_2 >= sqrt(3/2) is not established for all such C as written.

failure_location.quote: For matrices $\hat{\mc}_{k-1}$ with $k-1$ columns, assume that $\|\hat{\mc}_{k-1}^{\dagger}\|_2=\sigma_{k-1}(\hat{\mc}_{k-1})\geq\sqrt{3/2}$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Re-scope the induction to submatrices containing a fixed overlapping pair; interlacing then gives sigma_k(C) <= sigma_2(pair) = sqrt(2/3), i.e., ||C^dagger||_2 >= sqrt(3/2), for every M-column submatrix, preserving the theorem and threshold.
issues.overall_effect: The proof of Theorem t_ssv (no PTAS for two-norm minimization of the pseudo-inverse) is incomplete as written; Theorem t_cd (no PTAS for the mixed condition number), which applies t_ssv's bound, inherits the gap.
issues.title: Pseudo-inverse two-norm no-PTAS proof: induction hypothesis is false for disjoint column pairs
issues.why_classification: Local re-quantification using the already-proven step; the statement, threshold and dependent t_cd survive unchanged.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: For matrices $\hat{\mc}_{k-1}$ with $k-1$ columns, assume that $\|\hat{\mc}_{k-1}^{\dagger}\|_F^2\geq k-1+\tfrac{1}{4}$.
For $k=2$, two distinct sets can overlap in one or in two elements.
Then any collection $\mathcal{K}$ of cardinality $k=M$ has at least two sets $\mathcal{K}_i$ and $\mathcal{K}_j$ with $i\neq j$ and a non-empty intersection.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof explicitly assumes 'any two columns of C overlap'. This premise is unestablished and false for the objects the gap argument must bound: in a false X3C instance with M >= 3, an M-column submatrix can contain disjoint column pairs (disjoint sets can exist without any exact cover). Under the assumption the induction would be valid, but without it the induction hypothesis 'for matrices hat C_{k-1} with k-1 columns, ||hat C_{k-1}^dagger||_F^2 >= k-1+1/4' is false (a disjoint pair has ||hat C_2^dagger||_F^2 = 2 < 2.25). The proof therefore establishes ||C^dagger||_F >= sqrt(k+1/4) only for the subclass of submatrices whose columns pairwise overlap, not for all M-column submatrices of a false instance.

failure_location.quote: Assume that X3C instance is false, and assume that any two columns of~$\mc$ overlap.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Drop the all-pairs-overlap assumption and apply Lemma l_fi along a chain that retains a fixed overlapping pair: ||C^dagger||_F^2 >= (M-2)*1 + ||[c_i,c_j]^dagger||_F^2 = M-2+9/4 = M+1/4 for every M-column submatrix containing such a pair, which exists in every false instance. All thresholds are preserved.
issues.overall_effect: The proofs of Theorem t_pi and, derivatively, Theorem t_pi3 (Schatten p-norm, which re-runs this argument) and Theorem t_fcond (Frobenius condition number, which cites t_pi) do not support their stated inapproximability thresholds as written.
issues.title: Pseudo-inverse Frobenius no-PTAS proof rests on the unjustified assumption that all column pairs overlap
issues.why_classification: The repair removes one unjustified premise and re-indexes the existing induction; Lemma l_fi and the step are already in place, and the theorem and both dependents survive with unchanged thresholds.
